results.title: Meet the front-runners to replace Lagarde
results.content: Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot bring long records in monetary policy — and sharply different memories of the Draghi years.

results.title: Britain’s spy agency doesn’t know where thousands of its memory sticks are
results.content: Intelligence agency GCHQ acknowledges its plan for keeping track of USB sticks and other devices with potentially sensitive data on were 'not sufficiently robust.'

results.title: Von der Leyen touts ‘associate member’ status for Canada over objections of EU capitals
results.content: Commission president’s speech contrasted with a statement by Germany's Friedrich Merz, who referred instead to an “alliance for the future” between the EU and Canada.

results.title: Canada to join EU network of supercomputers
results.content: The compute power team-up is a first step for middle-power cooperation on AI.

results.title: Former Spanish employment minister died in train crash
results.content: Fátima Báñez, who oversaw Spain’s controversial 2012 labor reform, was among at least 69 people killed in Wednesday’s collision near Toledo.

results.title: Lagarde’s bandages due to a ‘little skin cancer,’ not ‘kick-boxing in Thailand’
results.content: In a video to staff, seen by POLITICO, the outgoing ECB president says her coverings are due to "a little skin cancer that had to go."

results.title: Russian strike on busy train platform kills at least 14 in Dnipro
results.content: Moscow also struck residential districts in the Ukrainian cities of Kremenchuk and Chernihiv, killing multiple civilians including children.

results.title: EU will nationale Social-Media-Verbote stoppen
results.content: Brüssel strebt ein einheitliches Gesetz an, um den Zugang junger Menschen zu sozialen Medien einzuschränken, doch die einzelnen EU-Länder verfolgen unterschiedliche Ansätze und legen unterschiedliche Altersgrenzen fest.

results.title: Denmark wants to ban ‘turbo chickens’
results.content: "They simply grow too fast for their bodies to keep up," said the animal welfare minister.

results.title: EU tells capitals to halt their national social media bans for a year
results.content: Austria, the first country told to halt its national legislation, has lashed out at the order from Brussels meant to allow for the unified EU law to first be finalized.
